_do_not_hand_edit: Derived fields are regenerated. Only state, evidence_tier, promoted, notes are preserved across a regen -- record progress there and nowhere else.

queries.why: The exclusively-tactical set: in the forward closure of llm_tact_mission_start / llm_tact_frame / llm_tact_mission_end_return_to_strategic, and unreachable from the rest of the program once those three are blocked. Measured by gen_tact_closure.py (155 functions / 85,016 B), --check'd by lint_repo, and deliberately not re-derived here.

_outward_effects._note: Outward calls from the migration set into the domain's effect families. An `effectful` target DOUBLE-FIRES under shadow mode, because restoring the pre-state between arms does not un-send a packet or un-draw a dialog -- and the state comparison still reads clean, so the run looks green. `pure` targets must NOT be suppressed: they are the negative arm that stops a seam from passing its own test vacuously. Dispositions are AUTHORED (see the domain's effect_classes file) and start unverified -- `verified` means someone read the body, not the name.

target_rows.name: time_GetCurrentTime
target_rows.class_why: Reads _G_LLM_GAME_CLOCK_RAW_TICKS (0x00e654e4, the deterministic SIM clock, not OS wall time despite the CRT-style name), FILDs it, FDIVs by a constant (DAT_0x00500204), FSTPs/FLDs the double result, and returns. No writes anywhere in the body.
target_rows.gate_why: TWO INDEPENDENT REASONS, either sufficient. (1) C4: the harness pin_wallclock replaces this entry outright (install_jmp, harness.cpp ~4093) and MH_Harness_Init runs BEFORE MH_Seam_Init (mh.c), so the pin always wins the entry -- and tools/test_ui.py's tact_write_config writes `pin_wallclock=1` into EVERY tactical ini, so a gate here would report PARTIALLY ARMED on every single tactical rig run and invalidate the whole banner. A permanent false alarm is worse than no line. (2) It is `pure`, so a gate can never suppress it; its only contribution would be INV-4 effect-log recording -- and with 24 program-wide callers a single shadow window would blow the 64-event log, which DISABLES the INV-4 verdict for that window. Gating it would cost the check it was supposed to feed.

target_rows.name: llm_fatal_cleanup
target_rows.class_why: Sets _G_LLM_GAME_MODE=0, then unconditionally calls a fixed sequence of teardown/shutdown functions: CoUninitialize (device/COM call at 0x0042615a), llm_gfx_free_draw_buffers, llm_gfx_planet_bank_free, FreeGlobalData, llm_strat_pathfinder_shutdown, llm_input_dimouse_shutdown, llm_input_di_keyboard_destroy, llm_gfx_font_unload/free_polalfa, llm_snd_shutdown, llm_gfx_release_display_surfaces, llm_net_shutdown_stub, and finally llm_game_clear_save_temp_files (deletes files) at 0x004261ac -- called immediately before utils::abort(0).

target_rows.name: llm_ui_set_draw_surface
target_rows.class_why: Own body (0x004a8b73-0x004a8be7) is nine unconditional MOV stores of its own parameters into globals (DAT_005d8b38/3c/40/44/48/4c, DAT_00603af4, _G_LLM_UI_SURFACE_PTR, _G_LLM_UI_SURFACE_PITCH) -- no read-before-write on any of them. It then unconditionally CALLs llm_gfx_blit_rect_rows (0x004a8bdc -> 0x004a66cc), whose body I decompiled: a straight per-row `memcpy(dst,src,w*2)` loop over the just-set globals, with the row counter reset from DAT_005d8b4c each call -- no accumulator, no LUT-blend, no counter that survives across calls.

target_rows.name: llm_rand
target_rows.class_why: Classic Watcom CRT rand(): dereferences the seed pointer from FUN_004da981, computes seed*0x41c64e6d+0x3039 (IMUL/ADD at 0x00426995... i.e. 0x004da995/0x004da99b), stores the new seed back (0x004da9a1), and returns bits shifted/masked from it. An accumulating LCG state store.
target_rows.gate_why: SAME TRAMPOLINE HAZARD AS llm_math_atan, and it was latent rather than observed. llm_rand's steal length is 6 and those bytes are `PUSH EDX` + `CALL 0x004da981` (the per-thread CRT data lookup) -- an unrelocatable rel32, so a gate here would have corrupted every draw the first time anyone ran with `pin_rand=0`. Under `pin_rand=1`, which tools/test_ui.py writes into EVERY tactical ini, no gate would have installed anyway: the harness LCG already owns this entry. BEING UNGATED DOES NOT MEAN UNMEDIATED HERE, and that is the point of the record this entry still gets: seams/harness.cpp's pinned_rand_next() calls mh::effects::enter_deferred() and honours the answer, so under the pin the draw happens in the ORIGINAL arm and is suppressed in ours -- proven on the rig by the TACTPROBE shared-effectful line (performed=1 suppressed=1), and mutation-checked both ways. THE RESIDUAL GAP, stated plainly: with `pin_rand=0` there is neither a gate nor a pin, so a shadow window over any of the six tactical callers would draw twice and shift the PRNG. No rig path sets it to 0; if one ever does, that run cannot be read as evidence about a rand-dependent body.

target_rows.name: llm_tact_ui_draw_player_row_list
target_rows.class_why: Body calls llm_ui_set_draw_surface directly (CALL 0x004a8b73 at 0x00435545 and 0x0043560e, once per branch of the per-row highlight/no-highlight split) for the row-highlight icon blit, in addition to calling the gated llm_ui_text_draw_rgb16 (CALL 0x0041be9d at 0x0043559f/0x004355d3) for the row label text. The text-draw reach is fine (stops at a gated target), but the icon-blit reach via llm_ui_set_draw_surface -> llm_gfx_blit_rect_rows is NOT gated, so the function's own body still performs an irreversible framebuffer write outside any gate. Per doctrine this makes the whole target effectful even though it also writes the tile-dirty state at the tail.

target_rows.name: llm_tact_vis_map_fill_default
target_rows.class_why: Nested loop that STOSBs the constant byte 2 across the entire _G_LLM_TILE_VIS_MAP_PTR grid (_G_LLM_VIEW_TILES_W x _G_LLM_VIEW_TILES_H): `STOSB ES:EDI` at 0x0043ac17, writing 2 unconditionally into every cell.

target_rows.name: llm_gfx_pack_rgb16
target_rows.class_why: Full body is register/stack-local arithmetic: reads global G_COLOR_FORMAT once (0x0043c58a CMP against RGB555) to pick a shift/mask formula over the three byte params, stores the packed value into a local (EBP-0x10), and returns it in EAX. No global or shared memory is ever written -- every MOV target in the disassembly (0x0043c581/84/87/bd/e9) is a stack slot ([EBP+...]), not a DAT_/G_ symbol.

target_rows.name: llm_tact_mark_view_tiles_dirty
target_rows.class_why: Leaf function, calls nothing (confirmed in the .asm -- no CALL instruction anywhere in the 0x20-byte body). It only does a REP STOSB memset loop writing 0x01 into a 20-row x 15-col region starting at [_G_LLM_TILE_DRAWN_MAP_PTR] (row stride 0x14=20, 0xf=15 bytes written per row, pad 5). That is a plain dirty-flag array write with no external effect at all -- it is the mechanism that makes the render pass redraw those tiles later, not a render/sound act itself.

target_rows.name: llm_ui_text_draw_rgb16
target_rows.class_why: Body writes _G_LLM_UI_SURFACE_PTR/_G_LLM_UI_SURFACE_PITCH from the current gfx draw surface (MOV [0x005d7190],EAX at 0x0041bec3 and MOV [0x005d7194],EAX at 0x0041becd) then calls llm_gfx_draw_text_blend_clipped (CALL 0x004a2c4c at 0x0041bedf), which is not in the gate list and performs the actual glyph blit to the framebuffer (its own callees are llm_gfx_font_draw_glyph_blend_clipped / llm_gfx_font_layout_text, both pixel-level draw routines). The irreversible act is reached directly, not through any gated target, so this is effectful, not state, despite the two surface-pointer global writes.

target_rows.name: w_sprintf
target_rows.class_why: Formats varargs through the shared formatter __uprtf (CALL 0x004e08d7 at 0x004d033b) into the caller-supplied `dst` buffer, then NUL-terminates it (MOV word ptr [EDX],0x0 at 0x004d0346). Every write lands in the caller's own output buffer, computed purely from the read-only format string + varargs -- e.g. the game's own text-scratch buffer (G_TEXT_TMP) per numerous src/mh_dll/libmh/sim/*.h comments describing it as writing 'only the non-hashed text-scratch buffer'.
target_rows.gate_why: A GATE HERE WOULD CORRUPT 61 CALL SITES. w_sprintf is __cdecl and VARIADIC; its entry in dll_call_protos.json is a derived VARARGS SHAPE (`from_varargs_shape` id `vi`, one int32 vararg) recovered for ONE sim call site. A gate re-pushes exactly the parameters the shape names and calls the trampoline, so every caller passing a different number of varargs would have the rest read off the gate's own frame instead of its caller's. The shape is fit for CALLING the function from one known site; it is not a signature, and a hook over the entry needs a signature. Nothing is lost by leaving it ungated: it is `state` (it formats into a caller-supplied buffer), so a gate would never suppress it.

target_rows.name: llm_tact_ui_sel_panel_draw
target_rows.class_why: Body directly calls llm_ui_set_draw_surface (e.g. CALL 0x004a8b73 at 0x00435117, repeated ~12x for the icon-slot blits across both single- and multi-mode branches). llm_ui_set_draw_surface is NOT one of the 31 gated targets: it stores the blit params into globals and immediately calls llm_gfx_blit_rect_rows() (verified by reading llm_ui_set_draw_surface's body at 0x004a8b73 -- CALL 0x004a66cc then CALL to blit), which performs the actual framebuffer write -- an irreversible screen effect. Since this irreversible act is reached via a function OUTSIDE the gate list, the doctrine's 'own body reaches it through an ungated function' clause applies, not the state-preserving parent clause. The five DAT_00713d1x/_G_LLM_TACT_TILE_DIRTY_FLAG_B writes at the tail are real state but are dominated by the ungated draw reach -- classifying this state would blind the oracle to nothing (the draws are the whole point) while under-suppressing a real double-render.

target_rows.name: GetResourseFilePtr
target_rows.class_why: The resource-load entry point: rsr_GetFileEntry(fileName) locates the pack entry, then the body does CALL file_seek (0x004cf0a9, repositions the pack's shared file handle), CALL utils_malloc (0x004cf0b4, fresh heap allocation), CALL utils_read_from_file (0x004cf0e1, real disk I/O into that buffer), and on an 'LZW' magic match a second CALL utils_malloc (0x004cf110) + CALL LZW_Decompress (0x004cf12a) + CALL utils_free (0x004cf135) of the first buffer.
target_rows.gate_why: SUPPRESSION IS AN ACCESS VIOLATION HERE, not a wrong answer. It returns a freshly loaded resource buffer and ALL FOUR of its tactical call sites dereference the result with no NULL guard: llm_tact_ui_sel_panel_init stores it into _G_LLM_TACT_SEL_PANEL_ICON_GFX and reads the sprite header at 0x00433f24/0x00433f55/0x00433f89; llm_tact_mission_load parses the POZ text buffer byte-by-byte (0x00437454), memcpys the MAP buffer (0x004376fe) and hands the GROUND buffer to llm_tlo_palette_convert_565_to_555, which read-modify-writes it 255 times from 0x0043c7cc. `state`/`pure` are no better: its irreversible leaves are a seek on the shared pack handle (0x004cf0a9) and utils_malloc/utils_free churn (0x004cf0b4, 0x004cf110, 0x004cf135), and NO declared region covers either -- the region named `file_ptr` is a different global (0x00520469, the ground/TLO palette pointer), not the pack handle. Performing it in both arms leaks the GROUND buffer every window, since only one of the two pointers survives the restore and nothing frees the other. So its callers are structurally un-shadow-armable and are proven OFFLINE instead, which is already what llm_tact_mission_load's ledger row records.

target_rows.name: llm_gfx_convert_pixels_565_to_555
target_rows.class_why: In-place RGB565->RGB555 squeeze over the caller's sprite_blob pixel array: for every pixel it reads *local_24 (MOVSX at 0x0043c84e), computes ((v&0xffc0)>>1)+(v&0x1f), and writes the result back into the SAME slot (0x0043c873) before advancing the pointer. The write target is also the read source of the transform, so the transform is applied to its own prior output on a repeat call.

target_rows.name: llm_tact_frame_cursor_and_reset
target_rows.class_why: Own body performs two irreversible display acts directly, not through any gated target: CALL llm_gfx_draw_cursor_ingame at 0x0042964c (which conditionally blits the cursor sprite into the live framebuffer via llm_gfx_blit_sprite_rle), then unconditionally CALL llm_gfx_present_flip at 0x00429651 (the DirectDraw surface flip that actually pushes the framebuffer to the display -- the canonical 'un-drawable' act). Neither llm_gfx_draw_cursor_ingame nor llm_gfx_present_flip is in the 31-name gate list, so this reach is ungated and the parent itself must be effectful (doctrine case a). After the two calls the function also loops over _G_LLM_VIEW_TILES_W*_G_LLM_VIEW_TILES_H tiles clearing _G_LLM_TILE_VIS_MAP's low bit and zeroing _G_LLM_TILE_DRAWN_MAP -- pure state bookkeeping, but it cannot be split from the irreversible calls that precede it in the same straight-line body, so the whole target is suppressed as one unit and the oracle is knowingly blind to that state slice for this target.

target_rows.name: llm_tact_unit_refresh_ui_slot
target_rows.class_why: Own body (0x00434f98-0x00435007) is structurally identical to llm_tact_ui_char_panel_row_refresh: it writes no global state, only reads _G_LLM_TACT_UI_SEL_PANEL_MULTI_MODE / DAT_00559098 / _G_LLM_TACT_SIDEBAR_SLOT_SCROLL / _G_LLM_TACT_SIDEBAR_SLOT_UNIT_IDS to find the matching visible slot, then CALLs the already-gated llm_tact_unit_draw_hp_bar_slot directly at 0x00434ff5 -- no intermediate hop this time. Since draw_hp_bar_slot is itself one of the 31 gate targets (classified effectful above, its own body does the pixel write), the reach stops there and this dispatcher performs no irreversible act and mutates no state of its own -- safe to run unsuppressed in both arms.

target_rows.name: utils_str_cmp
target_rows.class_why: Word-at-a-time string comparison using the classic 0xfefefeff/0x80808080 zero-byte-detection trick, reading through param_1 (EBX) and param_2 (EDX) only. Every instruction in both exit paths (LAB_004d1744: SUB EAX,EAX; LAB_004d176a: SBB EAX,EAX / OR AL,0x1) operates on registers only -- no memory store anywhere in the 0xa1-byte body.

target_rows.name: gfx_LoadSprite
target_rows.class_why: Body is four unconditional stores driven purely by the `id` parameter: sprite_data (0x0042655d, bank-pixels base + per-id offset), _G_LLM_CURSOR_PALETTE (0x00426577, bank-palettes base + per-id offset), _G_LLM_CURSOR_HOTSPOT_X (0x00426588, sprite-meta[id].origin_x), _G_LLM_CURSOR_HOTSPOT_Y (0x00426598, sprite-meta[id].origin_y). It calls nothing else (only utils_assert_stack_capacity) -- no draw, no blit, purely a cursor/sprite-pointer latch.

target_rows.name: llm_gfx_apply_resolution_change
target_rows.class_why: Own body directly (not through any gated target) calls llm_ui_info_media_draw_p2() at entry, which itself calls llm_ui_widget_list_draw() -- a real screen draw -- and later calls llm_gfx_apply_window_resolution(w,h), whose depth-2 closure is MoveWindow/SetCapture/llm_gfx_release_display_surfaces/llm_gfx_ddraw_set_display_mode/llm_gfx_present_flip/llm_input_dimouse_shutdown: an actual OS window resize + DirectDraw surface teardown-and-recreate + present/flip + input-device release. None of that is undoable by a state restore, and llm_ui_info_media_draw_p2 / llm_tact_ui_sel_panel_free_gfx are both ungated (only p1 and sel_panel_draw are in the 31). Double-firing on an armed shadow call would resize/reflip the real window and redraw the info panel twice while the state diff reads clean. The function also resets several globals (_G_LLM_GFX_VIEW_TILE_HEIGHT_PX, the whole _G_LLM_BANK_SPRITE_BASE table, glyph pointers) but per the doctrine those ride along inside the single recorded effectful call -- reserving effectful is correct here since the irreversible act is the function's own direct job, not something delegated through another of the 31.

target_rows.name: llm_gfx_apply_window_resolution
target_rows.class_why: Full OS-visible video-mode teardown/recreate: CALL llm_input_dimouse_shutdown (0x00428a2c), CALL llm_gfx_release_display_surfaces (0x00428a31, drops DirectDraw surfaces), CALL llm_gfx_set_window_resolution (0x00428a3c), then a real Win32 CALL dword ptr CS:[MoveWindow] on the game's hWnd for one of three fixed resolution branches (0x00428a60 / 0x00428a88 / 0x00428ab0), CALL llm_gfx_display_init (0x00428ac2), CALL SetCapture (0x00428acd, re-grabs the physical mouse), and CALL llm_map_cam_mark_viewport_dirty (0x00428ad4).

target_rows.name: llm_gfx_draw_text_rgb
target_rows.class_why: Own body sets position/color globals then unconditionally calls llm_gfx_font_draw_glyph_blend_clipped (0x004a2d08 -> 0x004a2fdc), which I decompiled fully: for each covered glyph pixel it reads the CURRENT destination pixel byte (`(char)*psVar14` at 0x004a30ba, used as a LUT index alongside the source coverage/color) and writes the LUT-blended result back into that same destination pixel (0x004a30de). That is a genuine alpha-blend read-modify-write against the framebuffer, not a plain overwrite.

target_rows.name: llm_gfx_font_select
target_rows.class_why: Body is four unconditional stores driven purely by the font_slot parameter: _G_LLM_GFX_FONT_LINE_HEIGHT (0x004a2544, table lookup by slot), _G_LLM_GFX_CUR_FONT_GLYPH_PTR_TABLE (0x004a2555, table lookup by slot), and DAT_005d81f4 set to one of two fixed constant addresses depending on a slot<1 branch (0x004a2560 / 0x004a256c). No prior value of any of these globals is read before being overwritten.

target_rows.name: llm_gfx_load_all_sprite_banks
target_rows.class_why: Own body (0x00465093, 41 bytes) is a bare 2-call sequencing wrapper: llm_gfx_load_sprite_bank_files() then llm_gfx_load_planet_extra_sprite_banks(). Read both callees' full bodies: each does GetResourseFilePtr (deterministic resource-file read) then a chain of REP MOVSD/MOVSB copies into global sprite-bank buffers (_G_LLM_GFX_BANK_PIXELS, _G_LLM_SPRITE_PIX_OFFSETS, _G_LLM_SPRITE_META, _G_LLM_GFX_BANK_PALETTES, _G_LLM_SPRITE_PAL_OFFSETS) plus utils_free and a call to llm_gfx_init_pixel_format (also read: pure loop recomputing palette words into _G_LLM_GFX_BANK_PALETTES_DARK plus a handful of scalar globals, zero calls). No blit, no DirectDraw, no sound anywhere in the closure -- this is a load-into-memory routine, restorable as a shadow region over the listed globals. The one UNGATED REACH hit (llm_gfx_load_sprite_bank_files, a wall not in this 31-name batch) is genuinely benign, not a sign the parent needs to be effectful.

target_rows.name: llm_gfx_sprite_pix_offsets_init
target_rows.class_why: Computes a single base address puVar1 = _G_LLM_SPRITE_PIX_OFFSETS[0] + _G_LLM_GFX_BANK_PIXELS (both globals it only READS, at 0x0049aca5/0x0049acaa) and then unconditionally stores 8 hardcoded word constants (1,1,1,1,1,1,1,0xffff) into puVar1[0..7] (0x0049acb8..0x0049acf6). Nothing at the target slot is read first; every store is a literal constant, not a function of the slot's own prior contents.

target_rows.name: llm_gfx_view_metrics_init
target_rows.class_why: Recomputes ~14 globals (G_WIN_W/H, _G_LLM_FB_PITCH, _G_LLM_VIEW_TILES_W/H, _G_LLM_VIEW_RADIUS_W/H, DAT_00825044/48/50, _G_LLM_GFX_PANEL_ROW_SKIP, _G_LLM_GFX_VIEWPORT_ROW_BYTES, and 5 fixed plane-pointer globals) purely as arithmetic over WindowWidth (0x005202c8) and WindowHeight (0x005202cc), which it only reads, plus one intra-function reuse of values it just computed in the same call (G_WIN_W read back at 0x0044e1a8/0x0044e1ad after being stored at 0x0044e172 -- consistent within one invocation, not an accumulator across invocations). Read the full asm: no field is ever read-modified against its own value from a PRIOR call.

target_rows.name: llm_input_key_dequeue
target_rows.class_why: On queue non-empty, copies 14 bytes (MOVSD.REP, 0x004d1058) from the ring slot into the caller's buffer, then increments and wraps _G_LLM_INPUT_KEY_READ_IDX (INC/AND 0x7f, stored at 0x004d1063) -- a queue-advance, i.e. consumes one entry.

target_rows.name: llm_input_key_queue_empty
target_rows.class_why: Reads _G_LLM_INPUT_KEY_WRITE_IDX (0x00e69db4) and _G_LLM_INPUT_KEY_READ_IDX (0x00e69dac), compares them, returns a bool via SETZ. No memory writes anywhere in the 0x18-byte body.

target_rows.name: llm_input_mouse_buttons_get
target_rows.class_why: Body is just MOV EAX,[0x00824fbc] (a cached button-state mirror written by llm_input_mouse_delta_pump) followed by epilogue/RET. No writes anywhere.

target_rows.name: llm_input_mouse_delta_pump
target_rows.class_why: Body accumulates into _G_LLM_INPUT_MOUSE_DELTA_X/Y (ADD dword ptr [0x005204d5]/[0x005204d9], 0x004266ce/0x004266d4/0x004266f2/0x004266f8) and drains the mouse event queue in a while(!empty) loop (CALL llm_input_mouse_queue_is_empty @0x00426699, CALL llm_input_mouse_pop_event @0x004266a5) -- a real queue consumer, not idempotent. Overwrites cursor globals _G_LLM_CURSOR_X/Y each iteration and per src/mh_dll/mh/seams/video.cpp:1173 also re-warps the OS cursor via SetCursorPos on frames the OS cursor is hidden.

target_rows.name: llm_math_atan
target_rows.class_why: Entire body is FLD double ptr [ESP+4]; CALL IF@ATAN (the Watcom FPU/CRT atan helper); RET 0x8 -- a thin wrapper around a pure math library routine. No memory writes.
target_rows.gate_why: ITS STOLEN BYTES CONTAIN A CALL rel32, SO A TRAMPOLINE OVER IT IS CORRUPT. llm_math_atan is 12 bytes at 0x004daa52 and its committed steal length is 9: `FLD qword ptr [ESP+4]` (4 bytes) followed by `CALL 0x004daa28` (5). mh::hook::install_trampoline copies the stolen bytes VERBATIM into a fresh allocation and relocates nothing, so the copied CALL branches by the original displacement from the new address -- somewhere arbitrary. MEASURED, not feared: gating it made llm_tact_calc_dir24's every atan leave the program, the tactical mission ended after frame 1, and `--tact-determinism` reported '0 frames' with NO crash dump -- a verdict that reads like a scenario problem and says nothing about a hook. Bisected to this one target on 2026-08-27. The class is `pure`, so nothing is lost: a gate would never have suppressed it, and its only contribution would have been INV-4 recording. tools/dump_steal_relbranch.py now measures this property for every proto in Ghidra and gen_dll_effects.py refuses to gate a flagged target (and refuses to run at all if one is missing from that file).

target_rows.name: llm_snd_ambient_reseed_planet_event_times
target_rows.class_why: Loop of 20 iterations, each computing a delay via utils_math_trunc then CALL llm_rand_below_fx at 0x0045e2d7, storing the draw into events[i].next_time via FSTP at 0x0045e2f2 (next_time = rand_draw + current_time).

target_rows.name: llm_snd_play_matching_sample
target_rows.class_why: Scans a 0x2c-stride sound-slot table with strncmp (CALL 0x004e14c0 at 0x004d2b8e) and on a name match dispatches to CALL llm_snd_channel_configure_voice_and_play at 0x004d2ba8.

target_rows.name: llm_snd_stop_all_channels
target_rows.class_why: Own body loops over every sound channel and calls llm_snd_release_channel_voice(i) directly (CALL at 0x0042ef50) -- that callee is NOT one of the 31 gate-list targets, and it issues real DirectSound vtable calls (Stop at vtable+0x24, conditionally +0x48, then Release at vtable+8, read at 0x004d2714-0x004d2756 in the callee) on the channel's live IDirectSoundBuffer. That is an irreversible COM/audio-device action a state restore cannot undo. The function also zeroes each channel's retrigger-time bookkeeping (state), but since the irreversible reach lands on an UNGATED function rather than another of the 31, the doctrine's state-not-effectful exception does not apply -- this is a target whose own body performs (via a direct, non-gated call) the irreversible act.

target_rows.name: llm_str_ansi_to_wide_scratch
target_rows.class_why: Null-check then unconditional CALL (0x004cf412) to llm_str_ansi_to_wide(dst=&DAT_00660d24, src), which I decompiled: it strlen's src, calls Win32 MultiByteToWideChar(src,len,dst,len) to write the converted wide string into dst, then NUL-terminates dst[len]. All writes into the shared scratch buffer DAT_00660d24 are a pure function of the src string's bytes -- no counter, no queue, nothing read from the buffer before being overwritten.

target_rows.name: llm_strat_time_resync_and_tick

A function is in this ledger because someone once called it AI, and drops out the moment it is renamed -- so a misnamed function is silently in, and correcting the name silently removes it along with any progress recorded against it. See _reclassified_out for rows removed that way, and re-read a row's `callers_in_ai` before trusting its membership: a row with callers_in_ai 0 AND reachable_from_root false is only in this file on the strength of its name. Reachability here is UNCUT: a plain BFS from the root over the whole call graph. docs/ai-closure.md cut the BFS at ui/view edges (to keep the closure from swallowing render/audio at 779 functions), so it reports 155 ai-prefixed functions reachable and 63 not. This file reports more reachable (164) and fewer orphans because a path THROUGH a ui function still makes an AI function reachable -- the right test for 'does this need a caller-side hook', which is what batch E turns on. The two are not in conflict; they answer different questions. Layering is computed on AI-only edges, because only AI functions are ever armed and only they can nest with each other.
